title: CBSE Class XII Information Technology (Subject Code: 802) – Official Board Model Solved Paper 1
prerequisites: CBSE Class XII Information Technology (802) syllabus: Database Concepts with MySQL, Operating Web Based Applications, Core Java & NetBeans GUI Programming, Work Integrated Learning (WIL)
instructions: Please read the instructions carefully before attempting the paper.
This Question Paper consists of 23 questions divided into two sections: Section A (30 Marks) and Section B (30 Marks).
Section A contains Objective Type questions covering Employability & Subject Specific concepts. All sub-questions carry 1 mark each.
Section B contains Subjective Type questions covering short answer, code conversion, SQL queries, multi-table joins, and Java programming.
Calculators and electronic devices are not permitted.

sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 7 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) Which Indian government initiative serves as a secure cloud-based document wallet for issuing and verifying digital certificates and documents?
(a) DigiLocker
(b) IRCTC
(c) CyberSwachhta
(d) GeM
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (a) DigiLocker**

**Explanation:** DigiLocker is a key initiative under Digital India providing citizens with a cloud-based storage platform for authenticated digital document verification (Aadhaar, driving license, marksheet).
questions.hint: The digital document repository portal under Digital India.

questions.q:
ii) What is the main purpose of Work Integrated Learning (WIL) in IT education?
(a) To replace school textbooks completely
(b) To integrate academic theoretical learning with hands-on industrial workplace exposure
(c) To conduct theoretical written examinations only
(d) To purchase computer hardware for school laboratories
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) To integrate academic theoretical learning with hands-on industrial workplace exposure**

**Explanation:** WIL bridges academia and industry by enabling students to apply theoretical knowledge in real workplace projects.
questions.hint: Bridging classroom learning with workplace practice.

questions.q: iii) Mention one popular open-source relational database server and one Java Integrated Development Environment (IDE) widely used in schools.
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
- **Open-source RDBMS Server:** MySQL (or PostgreSQL)
- **Java IDE:** Apache NetBeans IDE (or Eclipse / IntelliJ IDEA)
questions.hint: MySQL for database and NetBeans for Java.

questions.q:
iv) In software project management, which phase involves creating entity-relationship (ER) diagrams, UI mockups, and database table structures?
(a) Requirement Definition Phase
(b) Design Phase
(c) Implementation Phase
(d) Deployment Phase
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) Design Phase**

**Explanation:** The Design Phase translates functional requirements into technical blueprints, including database ER models, table layouts, and graphical UI mockups.
questions.hint: The phase where architecture and schemas are blueprinted.

questions.q:
v) State whether the following statement is True or False:
"E-Governance portals operate 24x7 and eliminate the need for physical queues in government administrative offices."
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: True**

**Explanation:** E-Governance services provide round-the-clock digital access to public administrative functions, reducing bureaucratic delays and physical queues.
questions.hint: E-Governance offers 24x7 online access.

questions.q:
vi) Which of the following is an essential characteristic of every software project?
(a) It is perpetual with no ending date
(b) It creates a unique deliverable and has defined scope and resources
(c) It operates with unlimited budget and infinite staff
(d) It requires no planning or requirement analysis
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) It creates a unique deliverable and has defined scope and resources**

**Explanation:** Projects are temporary endeavors characterized by unique outcomes, defined timeframes, and finite resource constraints.
questions.hint: A project is temporary, unique, and bounded by resources.

questions.q:
vii) Identify the odd one out among the following software tools:
(a) Google Chrome
(b) Mozilla Firefox
(c) Microsoft Edge
(d) MySQL Server
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (d) MySQL Server**

**Explanation:** Chrome, Firefox, and Edge are client-side Web Browsers, whereas MySQL Server is a back-end Relational Database Management System (RDBMS).
questions.hint: Three are web browsers; one is a database server.

sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 6 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) Which cryptographic protocol is indicated by the presence of a green/locked padlock in the browser address bar during secure financial checkout?
(a) HTTP
(b) HTTPS (SSL/TLS)
(c) FTP
(d) SMTP
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) HTTPS (SSL/TLS)**

**Explanation:** HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts communication channels using SSL/TLS cryptographic certificates to safeguard sensitive credentials.
questions.hint: The secure, encrypted version of HTTP.

questions.q:
ii) Which of the following is NOT an e-commerce website?
(a) amazon.in
(b) flipkart.com
(c) wikipedia.org
(d) meesho.com
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) wikipedia.org**

**Explanation:** Wikipedia is a free non-profit digital encyclopedia, whereas Amazon, Flipkart, and Meesho are commercial retail shopping platforms.
questions.hint: Wikipedia is an informational encyclopedia.

questions.q:
iii) In an e-commerce application, what is the temporary storage area called where selected items are held before finalizing the payment?
(a) Wishlist
(b) Shopping Cart
(c) Cash Register
(d) Delivery Queue
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) Shopping Cart**

**Explanation:** A Virtual Shopping Cart holds selected products, computes line-item subtotals and discounts, and allows quantity adjustments before checkout.
questions.hint: The digital basket holding items for checkout.

questions.q: iv) Mention two severe operational risks faced by e-business platforms during festival sale events.
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
1. **Server Downtime / Crash due to Sudden Traffic Spikes**
2. **Cyber Attacks / Payment Gateway Breaches by Malicious Hackers**
questions.hint: Server crashes from heavy traffic and cyber security threats.

questions.q: v) Name the official Indian railway portal used by millions to book online train reservations.
questions.answer: **Correct Answer: IRCTC** (`irctc.co.in` / Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation)
questions.hint: The Indian Railways passenger reservation portal.

questions.q: vi) A live, interactive online presentation or workshop conducted over the internet with real-time Q&A is called a ________
questions.answer: **Correct Answer: Webinar** (Web Seminar)
questions.hint: Live online seminar.

sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 7 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) Which of the following is an invalid identifier in Java?
(a) `total_marks`
(b) `_studentName`
(c) `2ndPosition`
(d) `$feeAmount`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) `2ndPosition`**

**Explanation:** In Java, identifier names cannot begin with a digit (`0-9`). They must start with a letter, underscore (`_`), or dollar sign (`$`).
questions.hint: Java identifiers cannot start with numbers.

questions.q: ii) What will be the output of `System.out.println(15 / 4);` and `System.out.println(15.0 / 4);` in Java?
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
```
3
3.75
```
**Explanation:** `15 / 4` is integer division yielding `3`. `15.0 / 4` is floating-point division yielding `3.75`.
questions.hint: Integer division drops the decimal part.

questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: `1`**

**Explanation:** `25 % 6` computes the remainder of 25 divided by 6 (`25 = 6 × 4 + 1` → remainder = `1`).
questions.hint: 25 divided by 6 leaves a remainder of 1.

questions.q:
iv) Which keyword is used in Java to declare a variable whose value cannot be modified after initialization?
(a) const
(b) static
(c) final
(d) immutable
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) final**

**Explanation:** The `final` keyword defines constants in Java (`final int MAX_STUDENTS = 100;`).
questions.hint: The keyword for constants in Java.

questions.q: v) Why is a `while` loop known as an Entry-Controlled Loop?
questions.answer: **Correct Answer:** A `while` loop checks the test condition **before entering** the body of the loop. If the condition is false initially, the loop body does not execute at all.
questions.hint: The condition is checked at the entry point.

questions.q: vi) What does WORA stand for in the context of Java's JVM architecture?
questions.answer: **Correct Answer:** **Write Once, Run Anywhere**
questions.hint: Java's core cross-platform philosophy.

questions.q:
vii) What is the default value of an uninitialized instance variable of type `boolean` in Java?
(a) true
(b) false
(c) null
(d) 0
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) false**

**Explanation:** In Java, instance variables of type `boolean` are automatically initialized to `false` by default.
questions.hint: The default boolean literal.

sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 6 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) A candidate key that is not chosen as the Primary Key is called the ________ Key.
(a) Foreign
(b) Alternate
(c) Super
(d) Composite
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) Alternate**

**Explanation:** Candidate keys that are not selected as the primary key are termed Alternate keys.
questions.hint: The secondary candidate key.

questions.q:
ii) In MySQL, what is the maximum number of digits stored before the decimal in a column defined as `DECIMAL(5, 2)`?
(a) 5
(b) 2
(c) 3
(d) 7
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) 3**

**Explanation:** Precision = 5, Scale = 2. Digits before decimal = `5 - 2 = 3` (Maximum number: `999.99`).
questions.hint: Precision minus Scale gives digits before decimal.

questions.q: iii) Write the SQL query to list all records from table `Hospital` where the department is 'Cardiology'.
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
```sql
SELECT * FROM Hospital WHERE Department = 'Cardiology';
```
questions.hint: SELECT * FROM Table WHERE column = 'value';

questions.q: iv) A table `Employee` has 6 attributes and 20 tuples. If 5 tuples are deleted and 2 new attributes are added, what are the new Degree and Cardinality of the table?
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
- **Degree (Columns):** `6 + 2 = 8`
- **Cardinality (Rows):** `20 - 5 = 15`
questions.hint: Degree = columns, Cardinality = rows.

questions.q:
v) Which SQL operator is used to test for missing or unassigned values in a column?
(a) `= NULL`
(b) `IS NULL`
(c) `== NULL`
(d) `LIKE NULL`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) IS NULL**

**Explanation:** In SQL, `NULL` cannot be compared with `=` because `NULL = NULL` yields unknown. `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` are used.
questions.hint: SQL uses 'IS NULL'.

questions.q:
vi) Which wildcard character in the SQL `LIKE` clause matches exactly ONE single character?
(a) `%`
(b) `*`
(c) `_` (Underscore)
(d) `?`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) `_` (Underscore)**

**Explanation:** In SQL, `%` matches zero or more characters, whereas `_` (underscore) matches exactly one single character.
questions.hint: The single character wildcard.

sections.type: Question 5 – Objective Questions (OOP, Arrays & Java API)
sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 7 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) Which method of `java.util.Arrays` searches a sorted array for a specified value using the binary search algorithm?
(a) `Arrays.search()`
(b) `Arrays.find()`
(c) `Arrays.binarySearch()`
(d) `Arrays.lookup()`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (c) `Arrays.binarySearch()`**

**Explanation:** `Arrays.binarySearch(array, key)` performs binary search on a pre-sorted array.
questions.hint: The binary search method in java.util.Arrays.

questions.q:
ii) What will be the output of evaluating `a = ++x * 3 + x++;` if initial `x = 4`?
(a) 20
(b) 21
(c) 19
(d) 24
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (a) 20**

**Step-by-Step Evaluation:**
1. `++x`: pre-increment turns `x` from 4 to 5, returning `5`.
2. `5 * 3 = 15`.
3. `x++`: post-increment uses current value `5`, then `x` becomes 6.
4. `a = 15 + 5 = 20`.
questions.hint: ++x gives 5; 5 * 3 = 15; + 5 from x++ gives 20.

questions.q:
iii) In Java, what command-line flag is passed to the JVM to enable assertion checking during execution?
(a) `-assert`
(b) `-ea` (or `-enableassertions`)
(c) `-test`
(d) `-debug`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) `-ea` (or `-enableassertions`)**

**Explanation:** Assertions are disabled by default. Running `java -ea ClassName` activates assertion evaluation.
questions.hint: The enable assertions flag.

questions.q:
iv) A constructor in Java:
(a) Must have a `void` return type
(b) Has the same name as the class and has no return type
(c) Must be declared with `static` keyword
(d) Is called manually using the dot operator
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) Has the same name as the class and has no return type**

**Explanation:** Constructors are specialized methods sharing the exact class name, lacking return types, and executing automatically upon `new` instantiation.
questions.hint: Same name as class, no return type.

questions.q:
v) What will be the output of `System.out.println("Barrackpore".indexOf('r'));`?
(a) 2
(b) 3
(c) 8
(d) 11
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (a) 2**

**Explanation:** In `"Barrackpore"`, indexing starts at 0: `B`=0, `a`=1, `r`=2. The first occurrence of `'r'` is at index `2`.

questions.q: vi) Name the root interface implemented when creating threads in Java without extending the Thread class.
questions.answer: **Correct Answer:** `java.lang.Runnable` (or `Runnable`)
questions.hint: The thread functional interface.

questions.q:
vii) Given `int[] val = {10, 20, 30, 40, 50};`, what is `val.length`?
(a) 4
(b) 5
(c) 6
(d) 50
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) 5**

**Explanation:** The array contains 5 elements. The `length` property returns total element count `5`.
questions.hint: Total count of elements in the array.

sections.type: Question 6 – Objective Questions (SQL Aggregates & Foreign Keys)
sections.description: Answer any 5 Questions out of 6 Questions. (5 × 1 = 5 Marks)

questions.q:
i) Which SQL clause groups rows that have the same values in specified columns into summary rows?
(a) `ORDER BY`
(b) `GROUP BY`
(c) `HAVING`
(d) `JOIN BY`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) `GROUP BY`**

**Explanation:** `GROUP BY` groups summary records for aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, AVG.
questions.hint: Clause used for categorical grouping.

questions.q:
ii) Which keyword is placed in a `SELECT` statement to eliminate duplicate rows from the query output?
(a) `UNIQUE`
(b) `DISTINCT`
(c) `DIFFERENT`
(d) `FILTER`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) `DISTINCT`**

**Explanation:** `SELECT DISTINCT column_name FROM table;` returns only unique non-repeating values.
questions.hint: The keyword for duplicate elimination.

questions.q:
iii) When creating a Foreign Key, what action automatically updates the matching foreign key value in the child table when the parent primary key is modified?
(a) `ON UPDATE CASCADE`
(b) `ON UPDATE SET NULL`
(c) `ON UPDATE RESTRICT`
(d) `ON UPDATE NO ACTION`
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (a) `ON UPDATE CASCADE`**

**Explanation:** `ON UPDATE CASCADE` ensures parent primary key modifications propagate to all dependent child records automatically.
questions.hint: Cascades updates from parent to child.

questions.q:
iv) What does the aggregate function `COUNT(*)` return in SQL?
(a) The sum of all numeric values in a column
(b) The total number of rows in a table including NULL values
(c) The average of values
(d) The total number of distinct non-null values only
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: (b) The total number of rows in a table including NULL values**

**Explanation:** `COUNT(*)` counts all rows returned by the query regardless of whether columns contain NULL.
questions.hint: Counts all rows including NULLs.

questions.q: v) State True or False: In SQL, the `HAVING` clause can be used to filter rows without aggregate functions before grouping occurs.
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer: False**

**Explanation:** `WHERE` filters individual rows before grouping, whereas `HAVING` is specifically designed to filter groups after aggregate functions have been applied.
questions.hint: WHERE filters before grouping; HAVING filters after.

questions.q: vi) Write the SQL query to find the highest salary from the table `Staff`.
questions.answer:
**Correct Answer:**
```sql
SELECT MAX(Salary) FROM Staff;
```
questions.hint: Use MAX(Salary).

sections.description: Answer any 3 Questions out of 5 Questions. (3 × 2 = 6 Marks)

questions.q:
Question 7
A local retail bookstore in Barrackpore wants to launch an online ordering website. List four essential features that the website must provide to ensure a convenient customer experience.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:** Four essential features:
1. **Search & Category Filtering:** Fast searching by book title, author, ISBN, and genre.
2. **Shopping Cart & Wishlist:** Ability to add books, adjust quantities, and save books for future orders.
3. **Multiple Secure Payment Methods:** Integration of UPI (GPay, PhonePe), Credit/Debit cards, and Net Banking over HTTPS.
4. **Order Tracking & Digital Invoices:** Real-time delivery status tracking and instant downloadable PDF receipts.
questions.hint: Search filters, shopping cart, secure payments, and order tracking.

questions.q:
Question 8
Explain two significant applications of Database Management Systems in the Banking sector.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
1. **Customer Account & Balance Maintenance:** Storing customer KYC profiles, active account balances, and real-time ledger accounting.
2. **Transaction Processing & Audit Logs:** Managing atomic funds transfers (NEFT, RTGS, UPI, ATM withdrawals) and maintaining tamper-evident audit trails.
questions.hint: Account balances and real-time transaction processing.

questions.q:
Question 9
Define the term 'Project'. Mention two characteristics that distinguish a Project from ongoing routine operations.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
- **Definition:** A Project is a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result.
- **Two Distinguishing Characteristics:**
  1. **Temporary Nature:** It has a specific starting date and defined completion deadline (routine operations are continuous).
  2. **Unique Outcome:** It delivers a non-repetitive, unique deliverable under constrained resources.
questions.hint: Temporary endeavor with unique deliverables vs continuous operations.

questions.q:
Question 10
State two critical precautions a user should observe when conducting online financial transactions on a shared computer.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
1. **Use Incognito / Private Browsing & Never Save Credentials:** Always decline browser prompts to save passwords or autofill card details, and close the session immediately.
2. **Log Out Explicitly & Clear Cache:** Click the official 'Logout' button and clear browser cache and cookies after the transaction.
questions.hint: Do not save passwords, use incognito, and log out.

questions.q:
Question 11
(i) What is the function of an E-Commerce Shopping Cart?
(ii) Name two popular Indian digital portals for citizen services.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
(i) **Shopping Cart Function:** Holds chosen items temporarily, computes subtotals with taxes and shipping, and directs users to checkout.
(ii) **Two Citizen Portals:**
  1. `digilocker.gov.in` (Digital Document Wallet)
  2. `parivahan.gov.in` (Vehicle Registration & Driving License Services)
questions.hint: Item holding/calculation and citizen service websites.

questions.q:
Question 13
Differentiate between the SQL commands `TRUNCATE TABLE` and `DELETE FROM` with respect to command category, execution speed, and rollback capability.
questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
| Feature | `TRUNCATE TABLE` | `DELETE FROM` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | Data Definition Language (**DDL**) | Data Manipulation Language (**DML**) |
| **Mechanism & Speed** | Deallocates entire data pages directly; **Extremely Fast** | Deletes rows individually and logs each row; **Slower** |
| **WHERE Clause** | Cannot use `WHERE` (removes all rows unconditionally) | Can use `WHERE` to remove specific rows |
| **Rollback** | Cannot be rolled back in standard MySQL DDL transactions | Can be rolled back inside active transactions |
questions.hint: TRUNCATE is DDL, fast, no WHERE; DELETE is DML, row-by-row, supports WHERE.

questions.q:
Question 14
A table `BOOKSTORE` has attributes: `Book_ID` (Integer PK), `Title` (Varchar 30), `Price` (Integer), `Category` (Varchar 20).

(a) Write a SQL statement to display Category and the Average Price of books in each category.
(b) Write a SQL statement to give a 10% discount by reducing the Price of all books in the 'Computer' category.
questions.hint: (a) GROUP BY Category with AVG(Price). (b) UPDATE SET Price = Price * 0.90 WHERE Category='Computer'.

questions.answer:
**Model Answer:**
**Console Output:**
```
Value: 3
Value: 9
Value: 15
Value: 21
```

**Step-by-Step Execution Trace:**
- **Iteration 1:** `x = 1` → prints `1 * 3 = 3` → `x` becomes `3` → `3 <= 7` is **True**.
- **Iteration 2:** `x = 3` → prints `3 * 3 = 9` → `x` becomes `5` → `5 <= 7` is **True**.
- **Iteration 3:** `x = 5` → prints `5 * 3 = 15` → `x` becomes `7` → `7 <= 7` is **True**.
- **Iteration 4:** `x = 7` → prints `7 * 3 = 21` → `x` becomes `9` → `9 <= 7` is **False** (Terminates).
questions.hint: x takes values 1, 3, 5, 7 and prints x * 3.

questions.q:
Question 16
A table `STUDENT_FEES` has attributes: `Receipt_No` (Integer), `Student_Name` (Varchar 40), `Course_Code` (Varchar 10), `Fee_Paid` (Decimal 7, 2).

(i) Write SQL code to insert a record: `1001, "Abhronila Sen", "IT802", 4500.50`
(ii) What is the total precision and scale of `Fee_Paid`? What is the maximum amount it can store?
questions.answer:
**Model Solution:**

**(i)**
```sql
INSERT INTO STUDENT_FEES VALUES (1001, 'Abhronila Sen', 'IT802', 4500.50);
```

**(ii)**
In `Decimal(7, 2)`:
- **Precision (Total Digits):** `7`
- **Scale (Digits after decimal):** `2`
- **Digits before decimal:** `7 - 2 = 5`
- **Maximum amount storable:** `99999.99` (₹99,999.99)
questions.hint: Precision is 7, scale is 2, maximum is 99999.99.

sections.description: Answer any 3 Questions out of 4 Questions. (3 × 4 = 12 Marks)

questions.q:
Question 17 [HOTEL Table SQL Queries]
Consider the table `HOTEL` given below:

Table `HOTEL`:
| RoomNo | GuestName | RoomType | CheckIn | DailyRent | Discount |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 101 | Debangshu Hui | Deluxe | 2026-01-10 | 3500 | 500 |
| 102 | Susmita Das | SuperDeluxe | 2026-02-14 | 5000 | NULL |
| 103 | Tuhina Paul | Suite | 2026-01-20 | 8000 | 1200 |
| 104 | Sachin Roy | Deluxe | 2026-03-05 | 3500 | 350 |
| 105 | Mahima Sen | Standard | 2026-02-18 | 2000 | NULL |
| 106 | Swadeep Ghosh | Suite | 2026-01-25 | 8000 | 1000 |

Write the Output for SQL Queries (i) to (iii):
(i) `SELECT RoomType, COUNT(*) FROM HOTEL GROUP BY RoomType;`
(ii) `SELECT GuestName, DailyRent FROM HOTEL WHERE Discount IS NULL;`
(iii) `SELECT SUM(DailyRent) FROM HOTEL WHERE RoomType = 'Suite' AND CheckIn >= '2026-01-20';`
questions.answer:
**Model Solutions:**

**(i)**
**Output:**
```
RoomType       COUNT(*)
Deluxe         2
SuperDeluxe    1
Suite          2
Standard       1
```

**(ii)**
Matching records (Discount IS NULL):
- Susmita Das: 5000
- Mahima Sen: 2000

**Output:**
```
GuestName      DailyRent
Susmita Das    5000
Mahima Sen     2000
```

**(iii)**
Matching records (RoomType = 'Suite' AND CheckIn >= '2026-01-20'):
- Tuhina Paul (8000)
- Swadeep Ghosh (8000)
- `SUM = 8000 + 8000 = 16000`

**Output:**
```
SUM(DailyRent)
16000
```
questions.hint: (i) Count per room type. (ii) Guests with NULL discount. (iii) Sum suites from Jan 20.

questions.q:
Question 18
(a) Write a complete Java program using a `while` loop that inputs a positive integer `N` from the user and calculates the sum of all odd integers from 1 to N.
(b) Differentiate between extending `Thread` class and implementing `Runnable` interface for thread creation.
questions.hint: (a) Use while loop with i % 2 != 0. (b) Multiple inheritance limitation vs decoupling.

questions.q:
Question 21 [DOCTOR & APPOINTMENTS Multi-Table Queries]
Consider the following relational tables:

Table `DOCTOR`:
| DocID | DocName | Department | OPD_Fee |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| D01 | Dr. R. K. Sharma | Cardiology | 800 |
| D02 | Dr. P. Sengupta | Neurology | 1000 |
| D03 | Dr. A. Banerjee | Orthopedics | 600 |
| D04 | Dr. S. Mukherjee | Pediatrics | 500 |

Table `APPOINTMENTS`:
| AppID | PatientName | DocID | AppDate | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1001 | Mamata Hui | D01 | 2026-03-10 | Confirmed |
| 1002 | Susmita Roy | D02 | 2026-03-11 | Confirmed |
| 1003 | Debangshu Pal | D01 | 2026-03-12 | Pending |
| 1004 | Tuhina Sen | D03 | 2026-03-12 | Confirmed |

Write SQL statements for the following:
(A) Display PatientName, Department, and OPD_Fee of all appointments confirmed with their respective doctors.
(B) Display all doctors whose OPD_Fee is greater than 600 in descending order of OPD_Fee.
(C) Add a new column `ContactNo` of type `VARCHAR(10)` to the `DOCTOR` table.
(D) Count total appointments assigned to doctor with `DocID = 'D01'`.
questions.answer:
**Model Solutions:**

**(A)**
```sql
SELECT A.PatientName, D.Department, D.OPD_Fee 
FROM APPOINTMENTS A, DOCTOR D 
WHERE A.DocID = D.DocID AND A.Status = 'Confirmed';
```

**(B)**
```sql
SELECT * FROM DOCTOR 
WHERE OPD_Fee > 600 
ORDER BY OPD_Fee DESC;
```

**(C)**
```sql
ALTER TABLE DOCTOR ADD ContactNo VARCHAR(10);
```

**(D)**
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM APPOINTMENTS WHERE DocID = 'D01';
```
questions.hint: (A) Join on DocID WHERE Status='Confirmed'. (B) OPD_Fee > 600 ORDER BY DESC. (C) ALTER TABLE ADD. (D) COUNT(*) WHERE DocID='D01'.

questions.q:
Question 23 [Java String Operations]
Consider the string variable: `String text = "Barrackpore Digital Hub";`

Write Java statements to perform the following operations:
(i) Extract the substring `"Digital"` from `text`.
(ii) Convert the entire string to lowercase.
(iii) Replace all occurrences of `'a'` with `'@'`.
(iv) Check if `text` starts with the prefix `"Barrack"`.
questions.answer:
**Model Solutions:**

**(i)**
In `"Barrackpore Digital Hub"`:
- Index of `'D'` is 12, Index after `'l'` is 19.
```java
String sub = text.substring(12, 19);
```

**(ii)**
```java
String lower = text.toLowerCase();
```

**(iii)**
